role.altitude: The photonics technician keeps aligning optics, running experiments and tests, judging results and failure modes, and capturing how calibrations are really done; reading values off instruments, computing losses by hand, typing test reports and drafting procedures from scratch shrink.
skills_to_grow: Setting up instrument links and test templates
Checking drafted procedures against instrument settings
role.ambitious_version: A technician whose bench records and reports every measurement, so more of the day goes into alignment and analysis.

tasks.short: Read and record photonic test data from the instruments, compute derived values, check results against the specification, and enter them in the test report.

steps.what: Technician reads instrument values and records photonic test data on the test sheet
Technician computes derived values: insertion loss, return loss, wavelength shift and beam quality
Technician checks results against the specification and judges anomalies
Technician enters the results in the test report

tasks.design: Power meters, spectrum analysers and interferometers on the bench are linked to test software that records each reading against the device serial and test step, instead of the technician copying values onto a sheet. The software computes derived values with fixed formulas and marks results outside the specification. The test report is generated from the recorded run, and the technician adds the judgement. Judging results stays with the technician.
tasks.previous_blocker: Values were copied from instrument displays and worked out in spreadsheets.
tasks.enabler_now: Test software that records data from linked instruments and produces reports.
tasks.still_hard: Older instruments without a data link.
tasks.human_edge: Noticing that a reading is off because a connector is dirty.

ambition.what: See drift across batches from recorded data instead of only pass or fail.

tasks.altitude: Much less copying and computing; judgement stays.

reach.learn: Whether recorded data reveal drift earlier.

evidence.claim: Test software records test data and produces PDF or Word reports.

assumptions: Boundary: recording and computing test data; running the tests belongs to the testing and experiment tasks.
Input contract for s1: about 70% of bench instruments have a data link to the test software; readings from the rest are typed into it; s1 is priced at that share.
Input contract for s2 and s4: the recorded run in the test software, with formulas and the report template kept by the technician.
unknowns: Share of instruments with a data link.
research_questions: Do transcription errors in test reports disappear?

incremental.description: Technician keeps instrument links, formulas and report templates current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: mostly older instruments; high: 70% of instruments linked.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Walk through the calibration on the equipment, document procedures such as calibration of optical or fiber optic equipment, have the engineer approve the final procedure and publish it.

steps.what: Technician walks through the calibration on the equipment and notes the actual steps, settings and photos
Technician documents the calibration procedure: steps, settings, tolerances and photos

loop.input: The technician's notes and photos and the instrument settings exported from the test software.
loop.output: A draft procedure in the lab's template with numbered steps, settings and tolerances.
loop.check: Every setting and tolerance must match the instrument export or the specification; the technician rewrites unclear steps.
loop.stop: The technician sends the draft for approval, or writes it by hand after two redrafts.
loop.why_not_simpler: Notes are shorthand and differ per instrument.

steps.what: Engineer reviews and approves the final procedure
Technician publishes the approved procedure in the document system

approvals.approved_version: The procedure version approved by the engineer in s3; any edit creates a new version that needs approval.

tasks.design: The technician still walks through the calibration and notes what is really done. A drafting step turns the notes, photos and the exported instrument settings into a procedure in the lab template, with every setting checked against the export or the specification. The engineer approves the final version in the document system, which publishes it with a version number and notifies the lab, instead of mailing files and keeping copies. Capturing the real steps and approving stay with people.
tasks.previous_blocker: Procedures were typed from notes and mailed around for approval.
tasks.enabler_now: Drafting checked against instrument exports and document systems with release workflows.
tasks.still_hard: Steps that rely on feel, such as fine alignment.
tasks.human_edge: Writing down the trick that makes the calibration repeatable.
tasks.altitude: Less typing and mailing; capturing the steps stays.

reach.learn: Whether current procedures cut calibration errors.

evidence.claim: Reports and procedures can be drafted by a model with figures from test systems, each figure traced.

assumptions: Boundary: documenting procedures; doing calibrations in production is outside.
Input contract for s2: instrument settings exported by the test software used in task 20384.
Walking through the calibration keeps its full time; the engineer's time is outside the technician's savings.
research_questions: Are procedures updated sooner after equipment changes?

incremental.description: Technician keeps the procedure template current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: unusual equipment with few exportable settings; high: standard instruments with full exports.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Book lab time and equipment, set up the optical bench, run experiment steps as directed, and discuss results to assist scientists or engineers in the conduct of photonic experiments.

steps.what: Technician sets up the optical bench: aligns lasers, lenses and mirrors
Technician runs photonic experiment steps as directed by scientists or engineers
Technician books lab time and shared equipment
Technician discusses observations with the scientist

tasks.design: Shared lasers and lab time are booked in a booking calendar that shows availability, instead of by mail. Setting up, running the experiment and discussing results stay hands-on. Recording the experiment data belongs to the test data task and is priced there.
tasks.enabler_now: Shared booking calendars for lab equipment.
tasks.still_hard: Experiments that change direction during the day.

evidence.claim: Booking calendars replace mail for shared equipment.

assumptions: Boundary: assisting experiments; recording test data (task 20384) and optimising process parameters (task 20387) are sibling tasks.
Setting up, running and discussing keep their full time.

incremental.description: Technician keeps equipment entries in the booking calendar current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: dedicated equipment; high: much shared equipment.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Read the test plan and prepare the setup, test optomechanical or optoelectrical products according to test plans, perform failure analysis on failed parts, and write the failure analysis report.

steps.what: Technician reads the test plan and prepares the test setup
Technician tests optomechanical or optoelectrical products according to test plans
Technician performs failure analysis on failed parts and determines the failure mode
Technician writes the failure analysis report

tasks.design: The failure analysis report starts from a template that pulls the test plan reference, the recorded test data and the part history, and the technician adds photos, the failure mode and the analysis. Preparing, testing and analysing failures stay hands-on. Recording the test data belongs to the test data task and is priced there.
tasks.previous_blocker: Reports were assembled by copying data and plan references by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Report templates fed from recorded test runs.
tasks.still_hard: Intermittent failures that do not repeat on the bench.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing the crack or contamination that explains the failure.
tasks.altitude: Less report assembly; testing and analysis stay.

reach.learn: Whether consistent reports show repeat failure modes.

evidence.claim: Test software records test data and produces PDF or Word reports.

assumptions: Boundary: testing and failure analysis; recording test data (task 20384) and diagnosing processing steps (task 16716) are sibling tasks.
Input contract for s4: test data recorded by the test software under task 20384.
Preparing, testing and analysis keep their full time.
unknowns: Number of failure reports per month.
research_questions: Do repeat failure modes get recognised sooner?

incremental.description: Technician keeps the report template current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few failures; high: many failures with standard reports.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
